pointers.sentence: It activates the language, and sets the request's attribute `LANGUAGE_CODE` to the code `get_language` then gives, the activated translation's, in lower case; the cache middleware keys a page by it (`django/utils/cache.py:_i18n_cache_key_suffix`).

Where the default language has no prefix, a `LocalePrefixPattern` gives an empty prefix only while that language is active, or none is (`django/urls/resolvers.py:LocalePrefixPattern.language_prefix`): with Dutch active, `"/arrivals/"` would not resolve.
With `USE_I18N` false it calls the functions of `django/utils/translation/trans_null.py`, which choose `LANGUAGE_CODE` for every request and activate nothing.
Django's documentation places `LocaleMiddleware` after `SessionMiddleware`, saying it "makes use of session data" (`docs/topics/i18n/translation.txt`).
Nothing in the middleware or in `django/utils/translation/` reads the session.
Its other rule stands: before `CommonMiddleware`, which resolves the path to decide on a slash (`django/middleware/common.py:CommonMiddleware.should_redirect_with_slash`).
`django.utils.translation.get_language_from_request` returns the first source that yields a supported code (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_language_from_request`).

**`LANGUAGE_CODE`**, through `get_supported_language_variant`, or as it is if even that fails, which the system check `"translation.E004"` reports (`django/core/checks/translation.py:check_language_settings_consistent`).

It returns the first whose lower case `get_languages` (`LANGUAGES`, keys lower-cased) holds and that `check_for_language` passes (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:get_supported_language_variant`).

`django.utils.translation.check_for_language` refuses `None`, and a code longer than 500 characters, before any cache is consulted, and asks `translation_catalog_exists` about the rest (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:check_for_language`).

Otherwise it asks the standard library's gettext module for a catalogue of the domain `"django"` for the code's locale in any of `all_locale_paths`: `django/conf/locale/`, each directory of `LOCALE_PATHS`, and each installed application's `locale` directory (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:translation_catalog_exists`).

Otherwise it asks the standard library's gettext module for a catalogue of the domain `"django"` for the code's locale in any of `all_locale_paths`: `django/conf/locale/`, each directory of `LOCALE_PATHS`, and each installed application's `locale` directory (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:translation_catalog_exists`).

These security releases added the length check before the cached lookup, "so that oversized, attacker-controlled values are not retained as cache keys", as the docstring says; the notes name the posted language of `set_language` as the way in (`docs/releases/6.0.8.txt`).

`parse_accept_lang_header` lower-cases the header, splits it with `accept_language_re`, written after RFC 9110 and RFC 5646, and returns each language with its weight, highest weight first, equal weights in the header's order (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:_parse_accept_lang_header`).
The docstring's reason: parses are cached, and a huge value kept as a key would use memory (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:parse_accept_lang_header`).

When a test overrides `LANGUAGES` or `LANGUAGE_CODE`, `reset_cache` empties the first two and `get_languages` ([Overriding settings](../startup/overrides.md)) (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:reset_cache`).

`LocaleMiddleware.process_response` sets Content-Language to the code `django.utils.translation.get_language` gives, with `setdefault`, so a view's own header stands (`django/middleware/locale.py:LocaleMiddleware.process_response`).
